keywords.def: an affectionate liking or fondness for someone or something
cause (a debate, conversation, fight etc) to start happening
frightened or nervous because of a lack of confidence

keywords.term: Oh my gosh! / Oh my God!
keywords.def: expression of feelings such as shock, surprise, anger, disbelief
make yourself smaller and don't use your full potential in order to make others feel comfortable
be vocal in defending or supporting a person who is being criticised or bullied

sentences.en: Hello.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: This is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English.
sentences.zh: 这里是BBC英语教学的《6 Minute English》。

sentences.en: I'm Neil. And I'm Beth. In this programme, we're discussing the positives and negatives of social media in the lives of young people.
sentences.zh: 我是Neil。我是Beth。在这个节目中，我们将讨论社交媒体在年轻人生活中的积极和消极影响。

sentences.en: And this is a really trending topic at the moment because of what's happening in Australia, where a new law to limit under 16-year-olds’ access to social media is being debated.
sentences.zh: 由于澳大利亚最近发生的事情，这是一个目前非常热门的话题，澳大利亚正在辩论一项限制16岁以下青少年使用社交媒体的新法律。

sentences.en: Neil, tell me one good thing and one bad thing about having social media in your life.
sentences.zh: Neil，能告诉我社交媒体在你生活中带来的一个好处和一个坏处吗？

sentences.en: Well, one good thing is it means I can see what friends are doing who live far away and one bad thing is it's really addictive and a massive waste of time.
sentences.zh: 嗯，一个好处是它意味着我可以看到住在远方的朋友在做什么，而一个坏处是它真的让人上瘾，而且极度浪费时间。

sentences.en: Well, it's interesting to hear a man's perspective, Neil, because when it comes to issues like cyber-bullying, it's often young women who are most affected, so soon we'll be hearing from women in different countries about their online experiences.
sentences.zh: 听听男性的视角很有意思，Neil，因为谈到网络欺凌之类的问题时，往往是年轻女性受到的影响最大，所以我们很快就会听到来自不同国家的女性关于她们网络经历的分享。

sentences.en: And remember you can find all the vocabulary and a worksheet on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 请记住，你可以在我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com 上找到所有的词汇和练习页。

sentences.en: But first I have a question for you, Beth.
sentences.zh: 但首先我有一个问题要问你，Beth。

sentences.en: In 2024, which was the most regularly used social media platform in the world?
sentences.zh: 在2024年，世界上使用最频繁的社交媒体平台是什么？

sentences.en: Was it: a) Facebook? b) Instagram? or c) TikTok?
sentences.zh: 是：a) Facebook？b) Instagram？还是 c) TikTok？

sentences.en: Oh, I'm going to say TikTok. Well, we'll find out the answer at the end of the programme.
sentences.zh: 哦，我要选 TikTok。好吧，我们将在节目结束时揭晓答案。

sentences.en: Now, let's start with the positive side of social media.
sentences.zh: 现在，让我们从社交媒体积极的一面开始。

sentences.en: As a politics student at Oklahoma University, twenty-one-year-old Haleigh Hurst campaigned in the 2024 US presidential election.
sentences.zh: 21岁的Haleigh Hurst作为俄克拉荷马大学的一名政治学专业学生，参与了2024年美国总统大选的竞选活动。

sentences.en: Here, she explains one benefit of social media to BBC World Service programme, Pick of the World: I do think social media has played a huge role in educating young voters on different policies and different people who are running.
sentences.zh: 在这里，她向BBC世界服务部的节目《Pick of the World》解释了社交媒体的一个好处：我确实认为社交媒体在教育年轻选民了解不同政策以及不同的参选候选人方面发挥了巨大的作用。

sentences.en: I know Trump has recently said that he has a soft spot in his heart for TikTok.
sentences.zh: 我知道特朗普最近说过他对 TikTok 情有独钟。

sentences.en: With the growth of social media it has sparked a lot more debates.
sentences.zh: 随着社交媒体的发展，它引发了更多的辩论。

sentences.en: I think my generation too has seen so many climactic things happen.
sentences.zh: 我也认为我这一代人见证了太多具有决定性意义的事情发生。

sentences.en: Haleigh thinks one good thing about social media is that it sparks debates and conversations – it causes debates to start.
sentences.zh: Haleigh认为社交媒体的一个好处是它能激发辩论和对话——它能促使辩论开始。

sentences.en: She comments that Donald Trump is a fan of social media by saying he has a soft spot for TikTok.
sentences.zh: 她评论说唐纳德·特朗普是社交媒体的粉丝，并说他对 TikTok 情有独钟。

sentences.en: If you have a soft spot for something or someone, you feel affectionate and fond of it; you like it a lot.
sentences.zh: 如果你对某事或某人“情有独钟”（have a soft spot），你会对它感到喜爱和温情；你非常喜欢它。

sentences.en: But of course, that’s not the whole story.
sentences.zh: 但当然，这并不是全部。

sentences.en: Increasingly, young women are reporting the negative impact social media is making on their lives, and the pressure they feel to appear 'perfect' online, especially from men.
sentences.zh: 越来越多的年轻女性报告说，社交媒体正在对她们的生活产生负面影响，她们感到了在网上展现“完美”的压力，尤其是来自男性的压力。

sentences.en: Maanvi Sharma, aged 28, is a businesswoman and model with a large Instagram following who lives in Delhi, India.
sentences.zh: 28岁的Maanvi Sharma是一位商人和模特，在 Instagram 上拥有大量粉丝，她住在印度德里。

sentences.en: And Kemi Adeyemi, is a twenty-six-year-old travel blogger from Lagos in Nigeria.
sentences.zh: 而Kemi Adeyemi是来自尼日利亚拉各斯的一位26岁旅游博主。

sentences.en: Both young women discussed these social media worries with BBC World Service programme, Pick of the World: … the person you're dating, they might leave you just because of the social media.
sentences.zh: 这两位年轻女性与BBC世界服务部的节目《Pick of the World》讨论了这些对社交媒体的担忧：……你约会的人，他们可能仅仅因为社交媒体就离开你。

sentences.en: They might think that you're not good for, you know, marriage like….
sentences.zh: 他们可能会觉得你并不适合，你知道的，结婚……

sentences.en: You can't be a good partner because you're on social media, because you're being watched by a lot of people, and they feel a little intimidated by this… "You know what, we saw your girlfriend - Oh my gosh!
sentences.zh: 你不能成为一个好伴侣，因为你在使用社交媒体，因为你被很多人关注，他们对此感到有点害怕……“你知道吗，我们看到你女朋友了——天哪！

sentences.en: She was wearing this, Oh my God! " But it's affecting my personal life… Some men or some people, they want you to shrink yourself so that they can, like, be the bigger person.
sentences.zh: 她穿着这个，天哪！”但这正在影响我的个人生活……有些男人或有些人，他们希望你“缩小自己”（shrink yourself），这样他们才能表现得像个大人物。

sentences.en: They get to listen to what your friends say about you, what your family says about you, and they are not able to, like, stand up for you, to say, "Oh, I know this person.
sentences.zh: 他们有机会听到你的朋友对你的评价、你的家人对你的评价，而他们却不能为你挺身而出，说：“哦，我了解这个人。

sentences.en: I believe she's not, like, doing these things for other reasons".
sentences.zh: 我相信她不是出于其他原因才做这些事情的。”

sentences.en: Maanvi thinks some men are intimidated by her popularity on Instagram.
sentences.zh: Maanvi认为有些男人对她在 Instagram 上的受欢迎程度感到害怕。

sentences.en: Intimidated means to feel frightened or nervous because you lack confidence.
sentences.zh: “害怕”（Intimidated）意味着因为缺乏自信而感到害怕或紧张。

sentences.en: She feels people gossip about her posts and photos, using expressions like, ' Oh my gosh!
sentences.zh: 她觉得人们对她的帖子和照片八卦，使用诸如“天哪！”

sentences.en: 'and' Oh my God! ' to express their shock or surprise.
sentences.zh: 和“我的天哪！”来表达他们的震惊或惊讶。

sentences.en: And Kemi agrees. She says that on social media, some people want her to shrink herself, a phrase meaning that you underuse your full potential in order to avoid making people uncomfortable, or to fit in.
sentences.zh: Kemi表示赞同。她说在社交媒体上，有些人希望她“缩小自己”（shrink yourself），这个短语的意思是为了避免让人感到不舒服或为了融入集体，而没有充分发挥自己的全部潜力。

sentences.en: When she's bullied online, Kemi says that these people don't stand up for her.To stand up for someone means to defend or support someone who's being criticised or bullied.
sentences.zh: 当她在网上遭受欺凌时，Kemi说这些人并没有为她挺身而出。“为某人挺身而出”（stand up for someone）意味着为受到批评或欺凌的人辩护或支持他们。

sentences.en: And I think it's time you revealed the answer to your question, Neil.
sentences.zh: 我想是时候揭晓你问题的答案了，Neil。

sentences.en: I asked which was the most regularly used social media platform in the world in 2024 – Facebook, Instagram or TikTok?
sentences.zh: 我问的是2024年世界上使用最频繁的社交媒体平台是什么——Facebook、Instagram 还是 TikTok？

sentences.en: What did you say Beth? TikTok. I'm afraid you're wrong.
sentences.zh: 你选了什么，Beth？TikTok。恐怕你猜错了。

sentences.en: It's Facebook, with over three billion regular users.
sentences.zh: 是 Facebook，拥有超过30亿的活跃用户。

sentences.en: OK, let's recap the vocabulary we've learned in this programme, starting with the verb spark, meaning to cause something, such as a debate or argument, to start happening.
sentences.zh: 好的，让我们回顾一下我们在本节目中学到的词汇，从动词“激发”（spark）开始，意思是让某事（如辩论或争论）开始发生。

sentences.en: If you have a soft spot for someone, you feel affection for them; you like them very much.
sentences.zh: 如果你对某人“情有独钟”（have a soft spot），你就会对他们产生喜爱之情；你非常喜欢他们。

sentences.en: To be intimidated means to feel frightened or nervous because you lack confidence in a situation.
sentences.zh: “感到害怕”（Intimidated）意味着在某种情况下因为缺乏自信而感到害怕或紧张。

sentences.en: The expressions ' Oh my gosh! 'and' Oh my God!
sentences.zh: 短语“天哪！”和“我的天哪！”

sentences.en: 'are exclamations of strong feelings like shock, surprise, anger or disbelief.
sentences.zh: 是表达震惊、惊讶、愤怒或怀疑等强烈感受的感叹词。

sentences.en: If you shrink yourself, you make yourself smaller and don't use your full potential in order to make others feel comfortable, or to fit in with them.
sentences.zh: 如果你“缩小自己”（shrink yourself），你会让自己变得渺小，不充分发挥自己的全部潜力，以此让其他人感到舒服，或者融入他们。

sentences.en: And finally, to stand up for someone means to be vocal in defending a person who is being bullied.
sentences.zh: 最后，“为某人挺身而出”（stand up for someone）意味着大声疾呼地为受到欺凌的人辩护。

sentences.en: Once again, our time is up! But if you're ready for more, head over to the BBC Learning English website to try the worksheet with a quiz for this programme!
sentences.zh: 又到了节目尾声！如果你还想了解更多，快去 BBC Learning English 网站，尝试本节课的测试练习页吧！

sentences.en: See you there soon! Goodbye!
sentences.zh: 很快再见！再见！
